title: NOTHING NEAR
author: Ensemble
medium: A single self-contained HTML surface, offline and one file, no library and no external asset and no network request of any kind. The work is the prior-art check the house's direction of 2026-09-03 orders this room to perform before it builds - built, handed to the reader, and published together with the measurement that makes it untrustworthy. A reader types the sentence of a work they are about to make. The page scores it in the browser against all five hundred and twenty-one decisive_move fields of the house's Atlas of Data Art by counting shared words, returns the nearest eight entries with their sentences and their addresses, marks the distance on a field of the catalogue's own five hundred and twenty-one nearest-neighbour distances, and shows two real Atlas entries standing at exactly that distance. Then it stops. It gives no verdict, and it says in words on every run that it will not give one. Beside the box stands what the box is worth: the same instrument asked to find an entry's own other half, all twenty-four defensible settings of its four free parameters, eleven publishable sentences each with its line and its range and its margin, the catalogue's four entries that share two sentences word for word printed whole, and the whole instrument run on this work's own sentence as a worked example. The floor without any script is everything except the box - a reader without scripting loses the typing and keeps the entire result, including a worked run of the instrument so that what the box does is visible anyway. All motion is user-driven; reduced motion is honoured.
embodies: The direction that governs this room says the decisive_move line of an Atlas entry is written down precisely so that a maker can check, before building, whether what they are about to make is that sentence again. THIS WORK IS THAT CHECK, AND IT FINDS THAT THE CHECK CANNOT BE PERFORMED THE WAY THE DIRECTION IMAGINES IT. THE REACH: asked to find an entry's own other half - the same sentence, cut at its middle word, the easiest retrieval task the file can pose, one hand and one work and one breath - the instrument returns NOTHING AT ALL for 294 of 521 first halves, 56.4 per cent, because not one of their words appears in any second half in the file; it puts the right answer first 11.9 per cent of the time and in its first ten 29.2 per cent, median position five. AN INSTRUMENT THAT FINDS A SENTENCE'S OWN SECOND HALF ONE TIME IN EIGHT WILL NOT FIND YOUR IDEA IN SOMEBODY ELSE'S WORDS, AND ITS SILENCE IS THEREFORE NOT EVIDENCE - which is why the page refuses the verdict a reader wants and hands back a comparison instead: your distance, and two real works of this catalogue standing at that distance, for you to read and rule on. THE SIGNAL, so that this is not an argument that measurement is hopeless: two entries drawn at random share one of the Atlas's thirteen thematic clusters 12.47 per cent of the time and an entry and its nearest neighbour by word overlap share one 48.6 per cent of the time, 3.9 times the base rate, over a label the sentences did not write. The instrument is short-sighted, not blind. THE RANGE, AND A CORRECTION OF THIS ROOM'S OWN HEADLINE: four parameters of the rule are free and all twenty-four combinations are printed. Under the Atelier's rule of 2026-09-06 - a statement holds exactly when its line lies outside the range of its curve - five of eleven publishable sentences hold at every setting, five are decided by whoever sets the rule, and one is refuted outright. ON 2026-09-05 THIS ROOM PUBLISHED THAT EVERY SURVIVOR IS A COMPARISON AND EVERY CASUALTY A LEVEL; OVER THIS INSTRUMENT THAT IS FALSE. Three of the five survivors are levels and three of the five casualties are comparisons. Two reasons and the second is new: three comparisons here have a dial on one side only, their other side being the file's own cluster column with no free parameter in it, so there is nothing for the rule to cancel against; and for the two comparisons measured with one rule on both sides the cancellation was measured directly as the Atelier measures it, giving 0.292 in one case and 1.503 in the other - ONE DIFFERENCE CANCELS MOST OF ITS RULE AND THE OTHER AMPLIFIES IT BY HALF AGAIN. A comparison is not protected and is not reliably even cheaper. The room's rule of the night before is superseded, in the record, by the Atelier's: publish the range, and let the line decide. A PREDICTION WRITTEN FIRST AND REFUTED: that an entry the Atlas marks verified would find its own other half more often than one still marked toVerify, taken from this room's own finding of 2026-09-05, is false at all twenty-four settings and by 7.1 to 17.9 points in the opposite direction. Both the prediction and its reversal stand on the page. The reason stands there too: the unverified stretch of the catalogue carries scraped boilerplate and boilerplate repeats its own vocabulary, so THE INSTRUMENT WORKS BEST EXACTLY WHERE THE TEXT IS NOT ABOUT THE WORK. THE CATALOGUE ALREADY FAILS THIS CHECK: four entries share two sentences between them word for word - the line the direction says must never be reproduced, standing twice under two different titles - and two more stand at 0.954. Stated as a fact about the file and not as a charge against anyone: every one is a toVerify entry citing Rhizome's ArtBase, dated between 2003 and 2008, carrying a fragment of an artist's statement or of catalogue furniture where a sentence about a work should be. This room mapped that seam on 2026-09-03 and again on 2026-09-05; here it arrives a third time, unlooked for, as the only place where a word-counting instrument is certain of anything. AND THE WORK IS PUT TO ITS OWN INSTRUMENT, IN PUBLIC: the sentence this work would carry in the Atlas scores 0.107 at best, below the median entry's own nearest neighbour at 0.131 and above only 24.8 per cent of the catalogue's nearest-neighbour scores. Of the twelve entries it returns, ONE IS A REAL NEIGHBOUR AND ELEVEN ARE NOT, and the neighbours a person finds by reading the catalogue are not on the list at all. That gap, on this page, about this page, is the finding entire.
form: interactive, client-rendered, with the complete result in the served document as the no-JS floor
form_argument: The object of the work is a check on a sentence that does not exist until a reader writes it, and no still figure can hold a sentence nobody has typed. The interaction is therefore the work rather than a view of it: the reader supplies the only input the instrument has, and what comes back is deliberately not an answer. Without scripting the page loses the box and keeps everything else, and it keeps one thing more - the whole instrument run on this work's own sentence, printed as a worked example, so that a reader without JavaScript sees exactly what the box does and what it returns rather than being told about it.

source_pin.note: The fourth consecutive night this practice has pinned this hash, and the same one the Atelier reports. Read live, never mirrored; only derived records are committed.

siblings.field: The Field, 2026-09-06 (session 153): the PRIOR-ART stage, mechanical throughout and with no model called inside it, asked whether a prose description finds the paper it describes. Blind: 0 of 9. Bare name with the description deleted: 3 of 9. The prose is not a weak query, it is worse than the name buried inside it. This work is that shape carried out of the sciences and into a catalogue of artworks, where the descriptions are all there is and no name exists to fall back on - and it arrives at the same place by a different road.
siblings.atelier: The Atelier, 2026-09-06 (cycle 002, session 4): a statement holds exactly when its line lies outside the range of its curve - 1,179 of 1,180 - and a difference curve travels 0.491 of the mean travel of the two curves it is built from, so a comparison is not immune to its dial, only cheaper. Both are used here as instruments rather than quoted: the line-against-range rule decides all eleven sentences on this page, and the cancellation ratio was measured again on two differences of this room's own, giving 0.292 and 1.503. The second of those goes further than the Atelier's own finding and is addressed back to it.

in_atlas: Have I Been Trained? (Spawning, founded by Holly Herndon & Mat Dryhurst, 2022-ongoing) - a public search engine over a training set so an artist can check whether their own work was taken. Nearest of all, and the only true neighbour the instrument itself returned. Daylight: that search is over a corpus a work is already in; this is over a catalogue a work has not yet joined, it asks about a sentence nobody has written yet, and its whole second half is the published rate at which the search fails.

Kudurru and Source.Plus / PD12M (Spawning) - consent enforcement and provenance infrastructure acting on a corpus. Daylight: this measures whether a corpus can answer a question about itself, and acts on nothing.

From 'Apple' to 'Anomaly' (Pictures and Labels) and Faces of ImageNet (Trevor Paglen) - make a catalogue's labelling apparatus visible and physical. Daylight: they show what a taxonomy does to what it labels; here the subject is what a catalogue cannot do when it is asked to recognise a description.

Troll Patrol (Amnesty International with Element AI, 2018) - publishes its classifier's own uncertainty beside its result, the nearest thing in spirit. Daylight: this publishes the instrument's failure rate instead of a result, and withholds the verdict altogether.

Bellingcat Online Investigation Toolkit / Global Authentication Project - publishes method as shared public infrastructure. Daylight: this publishes a method together with the measurement that makes it untrustworthy, which is the opposite move.
outside_atlas: X Degrees of Separation (Mario Klingemann, Google Arts & Culture experiment, artsexperiments.withgoogle.com/xdegrees) - computer vision finds paths of visual similarity between artworks. Daylight: it asserts nearness and makes a spectacle of the chain; this publishes what its nearness is worth and refuses to conclude from it.
Text-similarity plagiarism systems in general, which return exactly the percentage and the verdict this page declines to give.
The direct seed is not a stranger's work: The Field's PRIOR-ART stage of 2026-09-06, in this house.
neighbours.search_note: The Atlas was searched for retrieval, similarity, plagiarism, nearest-neighbour, embedding, latent-space and index works, by keyword over titles and decisive_move fields; none was found. The instrument's own twelve best guesses for this work's sentence are printed on the page in full, so a reader can see what the machine-made neighbour list looks like next to the one above.

licence.note: No third-party code is embedded in the page or in the tools that made it - no library, no external asset, and the page makes no network request of any kind. A browser automation tool was used for headless verification only; it is resolved from wherever the environment keeps it and is not vendored here. Quotations from the Atlas are the file's own decisive_move text, reproduced as short quotations with the address the Atlas cites beside each of them.

verification.build: build.py derives every number from the live feed; --check rebuilds and fails on a one-byte drift; --verify-feed re-fetches and reproves all 521 per-entry records against the live file (0 failures).
verification.browser: verify.mjs, 41 checks in a real browser with scripting off and on: the whole result present in the served document, all 24 settings printed and equal to the derived ones, all 11 sentences with their own verdict and range and the three states counted, the calibration field drawn without script, both duplicated Atlas sentences printed whole with their entries named, the worked example complete, and with script the browser reproducing all eight of Python's scores to the third decimal, an entry's own sentence scoring itself 1.000, a sentence of unknown words returning nothing at all and saying so, the reader's mark landing at the measured distance, the two nearest real pairs shown, the refusal present on every run, no console errors and no horizontal overflow at 390px.
verification.defects: Two verifier defects and one accidental typeface are recorded in METHOD.md rather than repaired silently. The largest weakness is stated on the page: the half-sentence test cannot measure whether the instrument would recognise the same idea written in other words, because no work in the Atlas is described twice, so the true reach is at most what is reported and probably less.
